newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: OAU opens way for other Africans to seek UN post.
newsitem.headline: OAU opens way for other Africans to seek UN post.

text.p: The chairman of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) has opened the way for another African to be elected U.N. secretary-general, urging African leaders to submit other names after the United States vetoed Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
This appeared to break a deadlock following the Nov. 19 U.S. veto when African states still seemed reluctant to put forward other candidates while Boutros-Ghali remained in play.

"It emerges from my numerous contacts and the consultations I have made that, in order to preserve Africa's chances for a second five-year term of office, it is time for African States who do so wish to present other quality candidates, together with that of Dr Boutros Boutros-Ghali," OAU Chairman Paul Biya, the president of Cameroon, said in a letter to African heads of state or government obtained by Reuters on Monday.
"These states may refer directly to the Security Council and inform the current Chairman of the OAU," Biya said in his letter, dated Nov. 29.
"In view of the degree of urgency conferred to this issue, I would be most grateful if you could let me know your opinion at your earliest convenience," he said.

Boutros-Ghali's term expires Dec. 31 and the United States has vowed to keep using its veto if necessary to deny him a second term on the grounds that the United Nations needs new leadership to carry out reforms.

Boutros-Ghali's immediate predecessors -- Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru, Kurt Waldheim of Austria and U Thant of Burma -- all had two five-year terms and this has become an unwritten U.N. tradition.

Biya noted that a July OAU summit in Yaounde, Cameroon, asked him to approach U.N. members "so as to obtain a second five-year term of office at the Secretariat-General of the United Nations Organisation for Africa."
"During that summit, the candidacy of the present Secretary-General, Dr Boutros Boutros-Ghali, was recommended to that effect."

Biya said he accordingly presented this to the U.N. General Assembly on Oct. 24, 1996, adding: "All these steps were not successful, due to the veto of one of the permanent members of the Security Council."
He said that according to his information, "the council still seems favourable to the principle of a second term of office for Africa to the post of UN Secretary-general."
A number of African diplomats have been mentioned as possible candidates but none has been formally submitted.
As recently as a week ago, Ambassador Legwaila Joseph Legwail of Botswana, a Security Council member, told reporters: "We don't have any (new) list. It is composed of one person, Dr. Boutros-Ghali."

Among Africans spoken of as potential candidates are: Under-Secretary-General Kofi Annan of Ghana, who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations; Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy; Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference; OAU secretary-general Salim A. Salim of Tanzania; Foreign Minister Moustapha Niasse of Senegal, and Olara Otunnu, a former Ugandan U.N. envoy who heads the New York-based International Peace Academy.
